subject.title: Policy plugins cannot see resolved/served model identity at any blocking-capable hook (security impact: our confidentiality guard failed open)

question: Should OpenClaw expose resolved or served provider/model identity to blocking plugin policy hooks, and should that be done by extending before_agent_run or by adding a new post-resolve pre-dispatch hook?
rationale: Source inspection confirms a real enforcement gap, but the permanent fix changes a public plugin API and a security-sensitive provider/model policy boundary.

options.title: Extend before_agent_run
options.body: Add read-only provider/model identity to before_agent_run event or documented context consistently across CLI and embedded paths, with clear fallback semantics.

options.title: Add pre-dispatch hook
options.body: Create a new blocking hook after model resolution and before provider dispatch so policy plugins can enforce against the selected serving candidate.

options.title: Document current workaround
options.body: Keep enforcement based on configured agent-chain eligibility and document model_call hooks as observe-only audit signals, leaving per-turn served-model policy unsupported.

recommendation.title: Extend before_agent_run
recommendation.body: Add read-only provider/model identity to before_agent_run event or documented context consistently across CLI and embedded paths, with clear fallback semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking lifecycle gate originated in the before_agent_run work, so this is the closest current hook owner for the API decision.
